record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some equations and figure text have formatting/OCR artifacts, but the text continues through the conclusion, appendices, and references.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests sample-wise and model-wise test-error behavior using dropout, a different method from the original double-descent studies, and reports its effect on those curves.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own sample-size and model-size test-risk curves, and CNN test-risk curves with and without dropout. The eigenvalue results in Figure 2 and training-loss results in Figure 7 do not measure the claim's test-error behavior and are not rows. The reported figure curves are not accompanied by extractable point values.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own test-risk curves over sample size and model size (linear regression, random ReLU features, 5-layer CNN on CIFAR-10) with and without dropout. These bear mainly on V6, whether the peak disappears under tuned regularization, and on V1 through the CNN no-dropout curve.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that dropout at an optimal rate mitigates or eliminates sample-wise and model-wise double descent in linear regression, random-feature models and 5-layer CNNs. They support this with an approximate (Taylor/Neumann-series) result rather than an exact proof, and pose monotone sample-wise risk as a conjecture. They also speculate that batch normalization might alleviate double descent.
record.recipe_differences: The study adds dropout adjacent to the fully connected layer and examines its effect on test-risk curves; it does not reproduce the original studies' methods unchanged.
record.method_sensitivity: The results are examined at different dropout rates, and the CNN experiments vary label noise and optimizer alongside width.
record.peer_reviewed: Japanese Journal of Statistics and Data Science
record.problems: The monotonicity proof is approximate and the authors say they cannot definitively assert monotonic decrease from it. The experimental curves are presented as plots without extractable point values or reported uncertainty. The CNN dropout settings are not described as optimally tuned.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 1's separate sample-wise curves for its listed dropout probabilities were not entered individually; the figure provides plotted traces but the text does not describe each rate's outcome separately. Figure 6's 0% label-noise no-dropout trace was also not extracted because the text does not separately characterize its curve.

untested.parts: No test error over training epochs is reported.
No characterized sample-wise curve without regularization. Figure 1 plots weak-dropout traces but the text does not describe any test-error rise with more samples.
No capacity sweep across model classes past interpolation is characterized without regularization.
No effective-complexity measure predicting peak location.

Variance as a separate driver and multiple/triple descent are not analysed (multiple descent in Figure 5 is only deferred to Chen et al.). Only one noisy versus clean CNN comparison is made, and the clean no-dropout curve is uncharacterized.

missing.what: Sample-wise test-risk traces for dropout present-probabilities 0.4–0.995, including near-no-dropout traces where a peak would appear
No-dropout (γ=1.00) model-wise linear-regression curve and its peak or multiple-descent shape, which the authors mention
CNN 0% label noise, Adam, no-dropout trace
Random-features traces across dropout rates, including weak dropout

record.verdict_notes: Evidence is figure-only, with no numbers or uncertainty reported. The reader linked R1–R3 to V1/V3 as 'reversed', which misreads regularized curves as evidence against unregularized double descent; they belong to V6. The CNN paragraph on label noise closely paraphrases Nakkiran et al. (an original source), but here it is attached to the authors' own Figure 6. The CNN dropout rates are not shown to be tuned. Theorem 1 is an approximate theoretical argument for V6 and is not a row.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests model-wise behavior in linear regression and a 5-layer CNN, not across all deep-network settings or with a systematic sweep locating the interpolation threshold.
No test-error curve over training epochs or training time is reported.
The sample-wise experiments use dropout settings; they do not establish whether more data raises test error without dropout in the original settings.
The experiments do not establish a general double-descent curve across model classes as capacity grows past interpolation.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as a predictor of peak location across size, epochs, and sample count.

The study varies label-noise conditions in CNN experiments and evaluates dropout, but does not test variance as a separate driver, multiple/triple descent, or whether an optimally tuned regularizer universally removes the peak.
The study does not recast complexity using an effective parameter count or test whether that turns the second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.
